```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Although the vote was unanimous, the minority concurrent opinion issued by Scalia, Alito, Thomas, and Roberts implied those justices would vote against any state laws limiting anti-abortion “speech” in a “buffer zone”.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"If there is one more anti-abortion rights appointment to the Court, anti-abortion zealots may be able to harass, without any legal limitations, women seeking reproductive services and the providers of those services.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Conservative legislation restricting abortion services and denying public funding for reproductive services for indigent women, combined with physical harassment and even the murder of reproductive service providers, has put reproductive rights (including, but not limited to, abortion services) out of the reach of millions of women in the United States.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Those who cannot afford to pay for their birth control out of pocket if their employers deny coverage will face the biggest challenges in their lives.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The far-right political movement that produced these judges gained support from neoliberal Democrats who wanted to end “welfare as we know it”.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Leadership of both parties enacted “blame the poor” “welfare reform” policies that have led to 1.7 million children and 600,000 adults, mostly single mothers, living on only $2 per day per person.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
